misconceptions.description: Assuming an available, easy-to-reach group represents the target population
misconceptions.trigger: learner recruits colleagues or experts because they are available and treats them as the real audience
misconceptions.feedback: Ask who the design actually serves. A convenient sample of experts hides the friction your real, less-experienced users would hit.

misconceptions.description: Screening participants on a trait unrelated to the design risk being tested
misconceptions.trigger: learner screens on availability, age, or general interest rather than the experience that drives the usability risk
misconceptions.feedback: Identify the design risk first, then screen on the trait that exposes it (for example, prior tool experience for an onboarding test).

misconceptions.description: Treating AI-generated personas or simulated sessions as a substitute for observing real users
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports usability evidence drawn from synthetic personas instead of real participants
misconceptions.feedback: Use personas to design the screener and profiles, but collect usability evidence from real members of the target population.

misconceptions.description: Generalizing to the whole population from a sample that covers only one slice of learner variability
misconceptions.trigger: learner claims the design works for all learners after testing only frequent or only novice users
misconceptions.feedback: Bound the claim to the slice you observed, or recruit across the variability before claiming the design works for everyone.
